title: NeoRadar system policy
description: systems/<system>/policy.json: the per-system behaviour policy. Absent means every default, which is the client's existing behaviour. Each domain adds its own section here; every key is optional and documented by what it does, and an absent key keeps the existing behaviour.

correlation.description: How this system decides a track is identified. Every key is optional; an unknown enum value or a malformed code is a load error and the system loads on defaults.

mode.description: Which identification methods this system honours. always correlates every target, which is the existing behaviour.

requireDiscrete.description: A conspicuity, special or emergency code never identifies, even when it is the assigned code.

acceptPilotSquawk.description: When nothing is assigned, a discrete transmitted code is adopted as the assigned code.

doNotCorrelate.description: Codes that never identify, as literals ("7010") or inclusive ranges ("7001-7007").

maxDistanceFromRouteNm.description: Refuse an assigned-code correlation when the target is further than this from the filed route. Skipped when no route geometry is available.

minGroundSpeedKt.description: Apply the conformance gate only at or above this ground speed.

correlateOn.description: anyCode identifies a Mode S aircraft whatever it squawks; conspicuityOnly requires 1000.

unknownEquipment.description: What an equipment string that says nothing about Mode S means. byAircraftClass asks the server, and counts as not capable until it answers.

decorrelateOnCodeChange.description: A code-correlated track drops to uncorrelated when it changes to a code that is not the assigned or an emergency code.

scope.description: network needs the server; without it the check degrades to local.

afterSeconds.description: Position age after which the track coasts. 0 disables coasting.

special.description: Special purpose codes, in addition to the emergency codes.

conspicuity.description: Conspicuity codes, in addition to 1000, 2000, 7000, 7010, 1200 and 1202.

coordination.description: How this system runs the coordination dialogue at a sector boundary. Absent means today's behaviour, which is that every level at a boundary is either the one the coordination table states or one a controller proposed by hand, and nothing is ever agreed without a dialogue.

notification.description: Advance boundary information: announcing a flight to the sector it is coming to, ahead of anyone coordinating it, which is what puts it in that controller's inbound list before it is touched. Absent means no notification tier at all, which is the existing behaviour.

leadMinutesBeforeCoordinationPoint.description: How far ahead of the coordination point a flight is announced to the receiving sector. The European regional default is 15. Absent means a flight is never announced ahead of the boundary.

perPoint.description: A different lead time at named coordination points, for a boundary that needs more or less warning than the rest. Keyed by fix name, matched without regard to case; naming one fix twice is a load error.

preDepartureLeadMinutes.description: The pre-departure half of the tier: a flight on the ground at an airport one of your sectors is active for is announced this many minutes before its filed off-block time, until it is airborne, so it is in the departure list before it moves. Read through isAnnouncedDeparture. Absent means no departure is announced ahead of off-block.

release.description: Release: letting the controller who takes the flight next turn, climb or descend it before the transfer of control point without asking. Absent means this system does no releases at all, which is the existing behaviour.

enabled.description: Whether a controller may release a flight on this system. The kinds are always turn, climb and descent, each optionally bounded by a level.

pointOut.description: Point-out: the controller working a flight drawing another controller's attention to it, with nothing asked in return. Absent means this system does no point-outs, which is the existing behaviour and leaves a plugin's prenotes alone.

enabled.description: Whether a controller may point a flight out on this system. It goes as an OLDI PNT to a controller who has advertised OLDI and as the legacy #PC CCP:PT point-out to anyone else.

holdMinutes.description: How long a point-out stays on the receiving controller's screen. Nothing on the wire ends it, so time does; zero is a load error.

filter.description: The standard versus non-standard filter. A coordination whose level matches the standing agreement and which is made in good time before the coordination point is already agreed, and needs no dialogue; anything else raises one.

acceptanceImplied.description: Treat a standard coordination as agreed without a proposal, which is what a standing agreement is: a written agreement applied automatically, with no exchange between the two controllers. False keeps every change a dialogue, which is the existing behaviour.

standardLevels.description: The level the standing agreement states at a coordination point, overriding whatever the sector file's coordination table carries there. Keyed by fix name, matched without regard to case; naming one fix twice is a load error.

climbFt.description: The agreed level for a flight climbing through the point. Null means the agreement says nothing about a climbing flight.

descendFt.description: The agreed level for a flight descending through the point. Null means the agreement says nothing about a descending flight.

nonStandardAfter.description: How late a coordination may be made and still count as standard. With both keys absent, lateness alone never makes one non-standard.

minutesBeforeCoordinationPoint.description: Inside this many minutes of the coordination point, any coordination is non-standard and raises a dialogue however well its level matches.

distanceNm.description: Inside this distance from the coordination point, any coordination is non-standard. Applied alongside the time limit, whichever is reached first.

surface.description: The surface: what a ground position does on its own. The five SPEC-171 ownership states are always computed and read through surfaceOwnershipState and surfaceResponsibleController; this section switches on the behaviour around them. Absent means every default.

autoAssumeOnClearance.description: EUROCONTROL ITWP Baseline HMI 4.3.17: a push, taxi, line-up or take-off clearance issued to a mobile nobody holds assumes it, so the ground position never assumes as a separate action. Only a ground status THIS controller sets counts; another controller's change never assumes anything here, and a mobile somebody already holds is left alone.

movement.description: Tunes surfaceMovementPhase, the NOVA 9000 TMERS event list read as states (unknown, on stand, pushback, taxiing, holding, on runway, taking off, departed, airborne, approaching, landed). The phase is always computed, every batch, from the zones holding the mobile, its speed, the ground flag and its height above the field, with the previous phase as memory; this block names the zones and moves the thresholds. Absent means every default, which matches the UK zones and the lhr tag thresholds.

standZoneTag.description: The zones.geojson tag that marks a stand area, matched as a whole tag. Empty means no zone counts as a stand, so on stand and pushback are never produced.

runwayZoneTag.description: The zones.geojson tag that marks a runway strip, matched as a whole tag. Empty means no zone counts as a runway, so on runway, taking off and landed are never produced.

movingKts.description: Ground speed at or above which a mobile is moving: taxiing rather than holding, pushback rather than on stand.

rollingKts.description: Ground speed at or above which a mobile on the runway is in a runway movement, taking off or landed, rather than entered, lined up or crossing. Must be above movingKts or the system loads on defaults.

approachAglFt.description: Height above the field below which an airborne, descending mobile is approaching.

departedAglFt.description: Height above the field below which a mobile airborne off a take-off roll is still departed rather than airborne.

runwayMonitoring.description: Runway monitoring, the NOVA 9000 RIMCAS scenarios the data supports. Absent means off. Present, even empty, turns it on with every default: strips from the package's runway zones (tags runway and rwy-09L-27R, LVP twin lvp) else a rectangle from the navdata ends and width, the landing threshold from the navdata end plus displaced threshold. Core publishes rimcasStage, rimcasReason, rimcasRunway, rimcasTimeToRunway, rimcasCountdown and rimcasLowVisibility; the package colours Stage One, flashes Stage Two and lists the Impending Arrival Window. A number that would make the net lie is a load error naming the key.

strip.description: Where the monitored area comes from and how far it reaches.

zoneTag.description: The zones.geojson tag marking a runway strip zone; the zone must also carry the pair tag (runwayTagPrefix plus 09L-27R, either order).

lvpZoneTag.description: The tag marking the low-visibility twin of a runway zone, used while LVP are in force.

runwayTagPrefix.description: The prefix of the pair tag on a runway zone.

sideMarginM.description: Ground metres added each side of the navdata rectangle beyond the runway's half width. Only the navdata fallback uses it; a zone is drawn where the author drew it.

endMarginM.description: Ground metres the navdata rectangle extends beyond each pavement end.

restrictedZoneTag.description: The zones.geojson tag marking a restricted area: any mobile inside one is a Stage Two (rules.restrictedArea). Empty turns the scenario off.

occupancy.description: A mobile inside the area is on the runway unless it is flying over it.

maxGroundSpeedKts.description: An airborne mobile faster than this over the strip is an overflight, not an occupant (vSMR used 160).

maxClimbFpm.description: An airborne mobile climbing faster than this over the strip is an overflight.

oppositeDirectionDeg.description: Two moving occupants whose headings are within this of opposite, and closing, are head-on (rules.oppositeDirection).

arrival.description: The arrival prediction and its two windows.

lookaheadS.description: How far ahead along the track an approach is searched for, seconds. Must reach stageOneS.

alignmentDeg.description: How far off a runway end's approach bearing a track may be and still count as aligned.

minGroundSpeedKts.description: Slower than this and an airborne mobile is not flying an approach.

maxAglFt.description: Higher than this above the field and a mobile is not on an approach yet.

countdownS.description: The Impending Arrival Window rows, seconds from the strip, largest first and strictly descending. An approach beyond the first row plus fifteen seconds is not listed.

countdownLvpS.description: The rows while low visibility procedures are in force.

stageOneS.description: An arrival this close to a strip with an occupant is a Stage One for both.

stageTwoS.description: An arrival this close to a strip with an occupant is a Stage Two for both. Must be below stageOneS.

stageTwoLvpS.description: stageTwoS while low visibility procedures are in force. Must be below stageOneS.

rules.description: Which scenarios run; each is its own switch so a package imitating another A-SMGCS takes a subset.

occupants.description: Two or more mobiles on one strip: departure, line-up, crossing and opposite direction. Stage One, or Stage Two for a mobile faster than stageTwoSpeedKts and closing on another and for the one it closes on.

arrivalVsOccupant.description: An approaching arrival against a mobile on the strip, through the two windows.

closedRunway.description: Any mobile on, or approaching within stageOneS, a runway the controller closed (.dev rimcas-close) is a Stage Two.

oppositeDirection.description: Two moving occupants head-on along one strip are a Stage Two with their own reason, ahead of the general two-on-the-runway rule.

restrictedArea.description: A mobile inside a zone tagged strip.restrictedZoneTag is a Stage Two.

stageTwoSpeedKts.description: vSMR's rule: an occupant faster than this and closing on another occupant is a Stage Two; slower is a Stage One.

sounds.description: Sound ids from the package's sounds folder, played once per escalation; absent plays nothing.

stageOne.description: Played when a mobile first reaches Stage One.

stageTwo.description: Played when a mobile first reaches Stage Two.

stageTwoRepeatS.description: While any Stage Two stands, the stageTwo sound plays again every this many seconds; 0 plays it once per escalation, as vSMR did. NOVA keeps sounding.

runways.description: What each runway is monitored for, keyed "EGLL 09L/27R" or "EGLL/09L" (either designator names the pair). A runway with no entry gets unlistedRunways. Both flags off and the runway is not monitored at all.

arrivals.description: Predict arrivals to this runway and run the arrival scenarios.

occupancy.description: Track who is on this runway and run the occupancy scenarios.

unlistedRunways.description: What an active runway with no runways entry gets: monitored for everything, or ignored.

safetyNets.description: The alert board every safety net wears: the server's nets (BUST and CLAM today, MTCD and TCT later), the client's own (RIMCAS, RAM, the emergency squawk), merged into one ordered set per aircraft and read through alertKind, alertSeverity, alertText, alertOther, alertCount, alertAcknowledged, alertsMuted and the twelve per-kind severities. Unlike the other sections an absent one is the full default rather than off: the board shows only what a label, list or target already asks for, so a package that binds none of those keys sees nothing either way. Numbers a vAcc owns (what each server net triggers on) live in the hub, not here.

show.description: Hides a kind on this system. An unlisted kind is shown, so name only what this system has no use for: a tower hides mtcd and tct, an area system hides rimcas and afdas. Hiding never stops the server evaluating the net; .dev alert-info says which kinds are hidden and which the server advertised.

sounds.description: Sound ids in the package's sounds folder, played once when an aircraft's highest alert escalates. Absent plays nothing, which is what a package that authors no sounds gets.

info.description: Played when the highest alert reaches info severity (MTCD, TCT).

warning.description: Played when it reaches warning severity (CLAM, RAM, AIW, RIMCAS Stage One).

alert.description: Played when it reaches alert severity (MSAW, BUST, RIMCAS Stage Two, an emergency squawk).

alertRepeatS.description: Seconds between repeats of the alert sound while any unacknowledged alert-severity alert stands anywhere. 0 plays once per escalation, which is the default; NOVA keeps sounding, vSMR sounded once.

perKind.description: Replaces the severity sound for one kind, so MSAW can have its own tone.

acknowledge.description: What the acknowledgeAlert click action does. The colour always stays: acknowledging says the controller has seen the alert, not that it has gone, and a change of kind or severity re-arms it by itself.

silencesSound.description: An acknowledged alert stops driving sounds.alertRepeatS.

expiresS.description: Seconds an acknowledgement lasts before the alert re-arms. 0 never lapses.

priority.description: Which kind alertKind and alertText report when several stand on one aircraft, highest first. Kinds left out follow the listed ones in the default order, so a partial list cannot hide one. Severity breaks a tie within a kind, then the server's own priority field. Use the per-kind keys instead where a system wants each net placed by hand.

emergencySquawk.description: Raises an alert-severity Emergency on any aircraft squawking 7500, 7600 or 7700, with the condition and the code as alertText. Client-side and needs no server.

ram.description: Route adherence monitoring, evaluated on the client against the route expansion the server landed on the flight plan, so the numbers are the package's. It measures cross-track distance to the leg the aircraft is flying and raises a warning-severity Ram with the distance as alertText. The server is still the only route expander, so with no server there is no expansion and the net is silent rather than clean; .dev ram-info says which of the two it is. Absent is every default below, as an absent safetyNets section is.

enabled.description: False stops the net evaluating at all. Use safetyNets.show.ram instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

triggerNm.description: Cross-track distance from the leg's centreline that raises the net, TopSky's number. Must be at least clearNm.

clearNm.description: Cross-track distance the aircraft must come back inside for the net to clear. Below triggerNm on purpose: the band between the two is the hysteresis that stops an aircraft riding the trigger flapping every cycle.

confirmCycles.description: Cycles beyond triggerNm before the net raises. A cycle is cadenceS, so the default is 40 seconds of sustained deviation. Clearing needs no confirmation.

cadenceS.description: Seconds between evaluations. The net rides the 2 Hz position batch and skips the batches inside this window, so this is also what one confirmation cycle is worth.

maxDeviationNm.description: Beyond this the net says nothing: the flight is not flying that route at all and a permanent alert on it is noise. Must exceed triggerNm.

directInhibitS.description: How long an assigned direct-to the server has not folded into the expansion yet inhibits the net, because the legs still describe the old path. The bound is what stops a direct the server never folds leaving the net silent on that aircraft for the session.

aiw.description: Airspace infringement warning, evaluated on the client: a correlated track no controller is tracking, inside or about to enter controlled airspace, which is the most common real incident on VATSIM. The sector file carries no airspace class, so controlled airspace is every ACTIVE volume whose sector an online controller works, unless this package draws its own with zones tagged controlledZoneTag, which then replace the volume rule entirely. It raises a warning-severity Aiw naming the airspace. 'Not on frequency' is deliberately not part of the rule: a pilot's tuned frequency is in neither the position stream nor the datafeed, so neither half can evaluate it. Absent is every default below, as an absent safetyNets section is. .dev aiw-info prints the airspace set it used.

enabled.description: False stops the net evaluating at all. Use safetyNets.show.aiw instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

lookaheadS.description: How far ahead on the current track the net looks for an entry, TopSky's sampling. 0 monitors containment alone, which a system that dislikes predicted calls wants; the lookahead is also what keeps a track skimming a boundary from flapping, because clearing needs no confirmation.

confirmCycles.description: Cycles inside or entering before the net raises. A cycle is cadenceS, so the default is 10 seconds. Leaving clears at once.

cadenceS.description: Seconds between evaluations. The net rides the 2 Hz position batch and skips the batches inside this window, so this is also what one confirmation cycle is worth; the default matches how often a pilot client sends a position.

controlledZoneTag.description: A zone tag in datasets/zones.geojson that marks airspace this net monitors. Authoring even one such zone REPLACES the online-volume rule with the zones alone, which is how a vAcc says precisely which CAS it wants watched. Whole tags only, so no spaces. An empty string turns the override off and leaves the volume rule in force.

squawk.description: The squawk provider chain: the package's priority per provider name, providers it disables, the reserved codes no provider may hand out, the circuit codes, and a first-party HTTP allocator. A provider the package does not name keeps what it declared.

providers.description: Keyed by provider name as the provider declares it (Generic, Server, the HTTP allocator's name, a plugin's). Omission keeps the provider; disabling is explicit.

enabled.description: False removes the provider from the chain, logged with the system that did it.

priority.description: Replaces the provider's declared priority for ranking. Higher wins.

reserved.description: Codes never assigned whoever proposes them, in addition to 0000, 7500, 7600 and 7700.

http.description: A first-party HTTP allocator: one POST per request carrying callsign, origin, destination, flightRule, aircraftType, cruiseLevelFt and circuit; one JSON object back carrying the code.

name.description: Provider name in the chain. Default Http.

priority.description: Declared priority. Default 50: above the server, below a plugin's 100.

codeProperty.description: The response property carrying the code. Default code.

apiKeyEnvironmentVariable.description: Environment variable holding the API key, sent as a bearer token. The key never lives in the package.
